answer.reason: The opinion text was unavailable, but the pack's 10-Q names the Oregon Williams case, with a $79.5 million punitive award (about 0.06% of the $134 billion non-affiliate market value) that PM USA had partly provisioned for, so the money at stake is under 1%. The ruling is a punitive-damages standard in one individual case, so it does not directly govern a core product or pricing practice (even though it affects pending cases such as Schwarz and Bullock), and the 10-Q discloses it in the contingencies note.
